title: Key Account Technical Solution Consultant
description:
Primary Function of Position
The Key Accounts Technical Solution Consultant plays a critical role within Intuitive ’s Digital Implementation team. This role is responsible for the successful technical engagement, deployment, and long-term integration of Intuitive ’s digital solutions across Integrated Delivery Networks (IDNs) and other strategic key accounts.
Working in close partnership with Intuitive ’s Key Account Directors, this individual will serve as a trusted technical advisor to enterprise-level IT.
This individual is accountable for ensuring strategic alignment and a scalable implementation framework that advances customer digital adoption across Intuitive platforms and deepens Intuitive ’s relationship with key enterprise accounts. A successful candidate excels in executive communication, enterprise-level solution design, strategic influence, and cross-functional orchestration and alignment.

• Enterprise-Level Implementation Leadership: Lead strategic planning and delivery of technical integrations for Intuitive ’s complete digital portfolio across multi-site health systems, ensuring long-term scalability and alignment with customer digital roadmaps.

• Stakeholder Alignment & Governance: Define communication strategies, feedback channels, and governance structures that ensure transparent engagement across both executive and technical stakeholders, internally and externally.

Deliver compelling technical presentations-including digital vision, technical product overviews, data flow, and network topology diagrams-to accelerate approval and prioritization top-down.

• Performance Accountability: Develop and maintain standardized implementation toolkits for aligned IDNs to define repeatable processes for operationalizing efficient deployment of Intuitive products from the enterprise to the division and/or local hospital levels.

• Metrics, Reporting & Documentation: Track, document, and report progress to Intuitive partners, highlighting outcomes, barriers, and system-level opportunities to increase speed and scale of adoption.

• Develop and Support Key Opinion Leaders: Interface with data privacy, security, and IT executive leadership to build collaborative partnerships through HealthTech Leader advisory board and other platforms.

Required Skills and Experience

• 8+ years of experience in medical technology implementation, enterprise IT consulting, or digital transformation within healthcare

• Experience with enterprise account management or direct collaboration with strategic sales

• Proven track record working with large healthcare systems and IDNs at a corporate level

• Deep understanding of cloud-hosted SaaS platforms, networking infrastructure, healthcare data security, and PACS/EMR interfaces

• Highly effective communicator with a demonstrated ability to influence without authority

Required Education and Training

• Bachelors Degree
Working Conditions

• Comfortable working a flexible, dynamic schedule

• Able to enter surgical and other patient areas

Preferred Skills and Experience

• N/A

title: Nuclear Balance of Plant/Flow Accelerated Corrosion Engineer
description:
Description:
Structural Integrity Associates, Inc. (SIA) is currently seeking an experienced Engineer to join our Balance of Plant (BOP) group. This group provides engineering and consulting services for most phases of above-ground piping, buried piping, and underground asset integrity programs. The successful candidate will be responsible for providing subject matter expertise related to Balance of Plant BOP Asset Life Cycle Management.

The ideal candidate will possess a solid understanding of BWR and/or PWR systems, experience supporting utility-side Flow Accelerated Corrosion (FAC) or BOP program ownership, and the ability to translate degradation mechanisms into actionable engineering recommendations. Additionally, the ideal candidate will contribute as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) in inspection and degradation assessment/evaluation.

This position can be fully remote or based onsite at one of Structural Integrity’s offices.

Primary Responsibilities:

• Provide engineering support for FAC program implementation, including inspection planning, evaluation of degradation mechanisms, and wall-thinning assessments.

• Perform flaw evaluations and support application of ASME Code Case N-513 for buried and above-ground piping systems.

• Contribute to the development, integration, and implementation of Aging Management Programs (AMPs) for license renewal and subsequent license renewal.

• Analyze system and component integrity across BOP applications, with a focus on risk-informed programmatic decision-making.

• Interface with and contribute to the enhancement of our MAPPro software tools related to corrosion, FAC, flaw analysis, and cathodic protection.

• Support or lead proposals, scoping efforts, and client engagement activities aligned with SIA’s strategic growth areas.

• Collaborate with colleagues across SIA’s Nuclear business unit to develop and implement turnkey solutions that span FAC, CP, flaw evaluation, soil corrosivity, and program management.

• Develop client relationships and provide on-time, high quality deliverables.

Required Skills/Qualifications:

• BS in Mechanical, Nuclear Engineering or similar discipline. Master’s degree, PMP, and/or MBA desired.

• Professional Engineering (PE) Licensure or ability to obtain PE license desired.

• 7+ years of relevant experience in engineering program support for operating nuclear plants.

• Demonstrated experience with FAC programs, such as FAC Manager, CHECWORKS, or equivalent software, and nuclear plant BOP systems.

• Working knowledge of ASME Section XI and Code Case N-513, including flaw acceptance criteria and evaluation methodologies.

• Experience developing or implementing AMPs in support of License Renewal (LR) or Subsequent License Renewal (SLR).

• Familiarity with MAPPro or similar asset management software platforms preferred.

• Advanced knowledge of related engineering standards, techniques and criteria and ability to interpret and apply codes, regulations, and industry best practices.

• Broad understanding of BWR and/or PWR systems and familiarity with proper remediation tactics.

• Proficient in writing and reviewing technical reports and proposals, with exceptional verbal and written communication skills

• Proficiency with Microsoft office applications, including Word and Excel

• Ability to travel up to 15% or more, upon request

• Previous Business Development experience preferred

• US Citizen or Permanent Residency

Competencies

• Strong client interface to both foster new and strengthen existing relationships

• Ability to identify and capitalize on areas for market growth for both products and services

• Ability to grasp and tackle complex assignments

• Ability to provide expert technical consultation to other engineers and management

• Strong planning and project management skills

• Strong technical and organizational leadership skills

• Good oral and written communication skills, including ability to deliver presentations confide

title: Generative AI Associate - Flexible Hours
description:
Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.

Scope of the Role:
At Innodata , we’re partnering with the world’s leading technology companies to build the future of generative AI and large language models (LLMs). We’re on the lookout for smart, savvy, and curious Generative AI Specialist to join our global contributor community as part of our Subject Matter Expert (SME) on Demand program.
This is not a traditional full-time role. It’s a part-time, remote, flexible, project-specific opportunity designed for those who want to make a real impact-on their schedule. Whether you're a writer, linguist, educator, researcher, or just deeply passionate about language and logic, this role lets you contribute to cutting-edge AI development while maintaining control over your time.
You’ll be helping LLMs learn the intricacies of language and reasoning-not just how to write, but how to think. If you’ve ever dreamed of shaping the intelligence behind tomorrow’s technology, this is your chance.
This is more than just a gig-it’s a rare chance to help shape the future of AI from anywhere in the world, on your own terms.
What You’ll Own:

• Rating/assessing the performance of AI models or algorithms based on their output or behavior through a set of evaluative questions.

• Labeling elements of a piece of content rather than the content as a whole.

• Assigning predefined categories or labels to items.

• Evaluating the perceived quality and/or appropriateness of content

• Generating labels to advance understanding of a concept, trend etc.

• Creation of additional training data for machine learning models by applying transformations to the original data, such as modifying images (rotation, flipping, cropping), generating new text (paraphrasing, summarization), or altering audio/video signals (speed modification, pitch shifting) to reduce overfitting and increase dataset diversity.

• Reviewing data and identifying whether or not a product feature works as intended based on the project's guidelines.

• Labeling model outputs to identify if a piece of content is or isn't something. Examples: identify clickbait; identifying gaming videos; identifying branded content.

• Ordering or ranking items based on a set of preferences or criteria.

• Creating prompts or questions that will be used to generate responses from a language model or other AI system.

• Projects that evaluate the relevance of content based on a relevancy scale (1-3, 1-5, etc.).

• Generating responses to prompts or questions using a language model or other AI system.

• Rewriting existing text while preserving the original meaning, often to improve clarity or style and adherence to guidelines.

• Producing concise summaries of longer pieces of text or data.

• Converting spoken language or audio content into written text.

• Converting text or spoken language from one language to another.

• Gathering and compiling various forms of data to be used for training, evaluating, or fine-tuning the AI models. This may include text, images, videos, audio files, or other types of digital content.

You’ll Thrive in This Role If You Have:

• A Bachelor’s degree or higher in a humanities specialization is required. Advanced degrees are strongly preferred (Master’s or PhD)

• Professional or Expert level proficiency (C1/C2) in English

The expected hourly salary range for this position is $15 p/hour, based on experience, skills, and qualifications.

We are seeking a highly experienced, hands-on Principal Data Engineer to define and evolve the architecture, engineering standards, and operating model for our enterprise data platform.
This role is for a technical leader who excels at complex system design: translating business and analytical needs into scalable, reliable, secure, and maintainable data products. The Principal Data Engineer will lead critical architectural decisions across data ingestion, storage, transformation, orchestration, governance, observability, and consumption, while raising the engineering bar through mentorship, design reviews, and pragmatic best practices.
You will work across engineering, analytics, platform, security, and business stakeholders to create systems that make trusted data accessible, timely, and actionable at scale.
What You’ll Do
Lead Data Architecture and System Design

• Own the technical vision and architecture for scalable, resilient, and cost-effective data platforms and pipelines.

• Design end-to-end data systems spanning batch and streaming ingestion, transformation, data modeling, storage, orchestration, serving layers, and consumption patterns.

• Make and document high-quality architecture decisions, including tradeoffs involving performance, reliability, scalability, latency, security, maintainability, and cost.

• Define reusable architectural patterns for common data engineering challenges, including CDC, event-driven data flows, schema evolution, slowly changing dimensions, data quality, and multi-tenant or domain-oriented data models.

• Establish clear boundaries and interfaces between operational systems, data platforms, analytics layers, and downstream applications.

• Lead technical design reviews for high-impact initiatives and provide clear, constructive direction on implementation approaches.

• Identify architectural risks early and drive plans to mitigate technical debt, single points of failure, data inconsistency, and operational fragility.

Set Engineering Standards and Best Practices

• Establish and continuously improve standards for data engineering development, testing, deployment, documentation, monitoring, incident response, and lifecycle management.

• Define best practices for version-controlled data transformations, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, code review, automated testing, and environment promotion.

• Build a culture of data reliability by implementing standards for data contracts, schema management, lineage, observability, freshness, completeness, accuracy, and reconciliation.

• Champion security, privacy, access control, governance, retention, and compliance requirements throughout the data lifecycle.

• Develop practical engineering guardrails that enable teams to move quickly without sacrificing quality, trust, or operational excellence.

• Drive adoption of well-defined SLIs, SLOs, alerting, runbooks, and post-incident learning practices for critical data products.

Drive Technical Decision-Making

• Serve as a trusted technical authority for complex, cross-functional decisions involving data architecture, tooling, platform capabilities, and engineering investments.

• Facilitate technical discussions that turn ambiguous requirements into durable, well-reasoned solutions.

• Evaluate build-versus-buy decisions, platform technologies, and vendor capabilities using clear criteria and documented recommendations.

• Align architecture decisions with organizational priorities, business outcomes, data strategy, and long-term platform sustainability.

description:

Lyft is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace that fosters belonging. title: Salesforce Developer
description:
Salesforce Developer

We are seeking an experienced Salesforce Developer to design, develop, enhance, and maintain Salesforce solutions supporting a large-scale federal healthcare modernization program.

• Strong proficiency with Apex and Lightning Web Components (LWC).

• Experience with Salesforce Flow and declarative platform capabilities.

• Strong understanding of SOQL, SOSL, Salesforce data models, and platform security.

• Experience integrating Salesforce with external applications using REST and SOAP APIs.

• Experience developing solutions within Salesforce Lightning Experience.

• Experience with version control and source-driven development.

• Experience supporting Salesforce testing, releases, and production deployments.

• Knowledge of object-oriented programming and software development best practices.

• Experience working within Agile development environments.

• Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

• Previous experience supporting federal government, federal healthcare, or health IT programs.

• Experience with Salesforce Government Cloud or Salesforce implementations within highly regulated environments.

• Experience with MuleSoft or other enterprise integration platforms.

• Experience with Salesforce DX and modern DevOps/CI/CD practices.

• Familiarity with Azure DevOps, Jenkins, GitHub, or similar delivery tools.

• Experience supporting enterprise modernization and cloud transformation initiatives.

• Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I

About the role
The Salesforce Certified Administrator role is focused on ensuring the health, security, governance, and adoption of a Salesforce platform that supports Sales, Marketing, and business operations.
This role supports Salesforce administration, automation, data integrity, reporting, system updates, integrations, and user enablement across cross-functional teams.
As Salesforce Certified Administrator, you will partner with stakeholders to streamline business processes, optimize workflows, strengthen platform governance, and support ongoing adoption through training, documentation, and responsive user support.

• Ensure the health, security, and governance of the Salesforce instance through best practices and compliance standards.

• Maintain data integrity, de-duplication, and data security policies.

title: In-Home Health - Physician (Part Time) - Wenatchee, WA
description:
Job Title: In-Home Health - Physician (Part Time) - Wenatchee, WA
Job Location: Work at Home, Washington, United States
Job Location Type: Remote
Job Contract Type: Part time
Job Seniority Level:
We’re building a world of health around every individual - shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger - helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.
Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Part-time Physician to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.
You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.
Job highlights
The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.
In this role, you will:

• Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

• Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

• Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

• Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

• Conduct virtual visits as needed

• Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.
Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“Many of the people I see are shocked that a physician is coming to their home to visit with them one-on-one. When you sit down and have an unhurried conversation about their health, they are impressed, happy, and understand that their health plan and care team cares about them.” - M.L., MD
“The primary care physician gets a snapshot of a person in an office setting, but with Signify Health, we see things like the number of steps to enter their home, the state of disrepair those steps may be in, and the person’s ability to function comfortably and with ease in their own home. We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD

Part-time employees qualify for:

• Select benefits (see benefits guide for details)

• Malpractice insurance coverage (during Signify Health-related activities)

• Supplies and other perks

Required & Preferred Qualifications (MDs and DOs)

• Active, unrestricted license(s) in coverage area(s)

• Multi-state licenses (preferred)

• Able to cover the following primary locations: Wenatchee MSA -Chelan, Douglas and Grant

Company Background

Censys ’ mission is to be the one place to understand everything on the internet. Frustrated by the lack of trustworthy Internet intelligence, we set out to create the industry’s most comprehensive, accurate, and up-to-date map of the Internet. Today, Censys delivers real-time Internet intelligence and actionable threat insights to global governments, over 50% of the Fortune 500, and leading threat intelligence providers worldwide.

We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to scale execution of the Censys Internet Map: the most continuously updated view of every asset, port, service, and certificate we can find across the public internet. Building it means running one of the largest internet-wide scanning operations in the world - 400+ Protocols providing access to 3Trillion+ scans in our APIs, 10PetaBytes+ of historical data, scanning 250Million+ IPs across 65K ports daily, resolving 8Billion+ names every 24 hours and tracking DNS at scale, tracking 18B+ certificates, fingerprinting 100K+ technologies behind what we find, enriching all of it with human readable labels, and third-party context so it becomes actionable intelligence rather than raw data.

This role is anchored in disciplined delivery, translating complex coverage and enrichment priorities into requirements engineering can build against. You'll define business and customer priorities, run the delivery cadence, and keep engineering and cross-functional stakeholders aligned on what's shipping and why it matters.

What You’ll Do

Internet Map Execution: You will define the business and customer priorities behind what goes into the Internet Map and how it stays best-in-class. This is the lever that enables Censys to be successful across every product and every segment we operate in.

• Coverage: How do we grow the map, how often we refresh it, and how comprehensively? This spans expanding IPv4/IPv6 scan scope, adding and prioritizing ports and protocols, increasing scan and DNS resolution frequency, and improving certificate and host discovery. You'll define this data collection work as detailed engineering requirements and acceptance criteria, and track coverage against baselines to identify and close gaps.

• Context: How do we enrich data into actionable intelligence? You'll define enrichment priorities based on customer and product needs: technology fingerprinting, risk scoring, and third-party data integrations. This includes evaluating external/third-party data sources for accuracy, coverage, and cost; defining the metrics used to judge data and enrichment quality; defining the schema that structures how coverage and context data is represented; and writing the documentation that makes both understandable and usable internally and externally.

Cross-Team Alignment and Execution:

• Drive cross-functional data prioritization across the Censys suite and provide business priority input into sequencing for new protocols and enrichments, ensuring data investments align with company goals, resolve multi-product conflicts, and provide roadmap transparency to other product managers and EMs.

• Engineering partnership and data quality: You ensure Engineering teams working on scanning infrastructure, data pipelines, and enrichment systems have well-defined requirements, clear acceptance criteria, and the context they need to make good architectural decisions. Track coverage and context quality against baselines. Identify gaps between current state and target, and translate findings into concrete engineering work to close them.

• Cross-functional enablement: Peer product teams (Exposure Management, Security Operations, Critical Infrastructure, Platform) and GTM (Sales, Marketing, Customer Success) build on and sell your data. Keep both audiences current on what's shipping, what's changing, and what's coming next, through regular updates, enablement sessions, and technical documentation.

Wander is building the future of hospitality, helping travelers find exceptional vacation homes. We're looking for a Senior Product Designer with outstanding visual craft to help make Wander feel as remarkable as the homes and technology behind it.

You'll split your time roughly evenly between brand and product, working alongside our brand designer and partnering closely with Product and Engineering. This is a hands-on individual contributor role: most of your week is spent making things and shipping them.

What you'll work on

• Help establish a distinctive visual language for Wander through motion, illustration, and iconography.

• Design beautiful, intuitive, customer-facing experiences across web and mobile.

• Create brand moments for travelers and operators: campaigns, ads, launch assets, events, and presentations.

Who you are

•
Exceptional visual craft. You have a strong eye for typography, composition, color, and interaction design. Your work is thoughtful, polished, and unmistakably well designed.

•
Motion, illustration, and icons. You have real depth in motion or illustration, strength in the other, and the ability to draw a clean, consistent icon set. You use them to bring personality and delight to our brand and product.

•
Strong product thinking. You've shipped consumer products on web and mobile, and you can turn complex problems into simple, intuitive experiences.

•
A builder's mindset. You love prototyping, exploring ideas in Figma, experimenting with AI, and bringing concepts to life with tools like Vercel. Even better if you build your own tools.

•
An obsession with the details. You care deeply about design, from the overall experience down to the precise shade of gray. Sometimes a little too deeply. We get it.

We're a small, ambitious team that values experimentation, creativity, and strong opinions loosely held. We're looking for someone who can bring fresh ideas, elevate our visual identity, and make every experience feel more considered.

To apply, include a portfolio with shipped product work, plus motion, illustration, and icon samples.

Details: Remote in the US.

At a glance

• Exceptional visual and interaction craft, especially typography, composition, and polish.

• Demonstrated excellence in motion or illustration, strength in the other, and solid icon design. Not just a passing interest.

• Helps define a distinctive, elevated Wander visual language across product and brand.

title: Principal Engineer, Security Architecture - DGX Cloud
description:
NVIDIA DGX Cloudis an AI Factory designed to power the next generation of AI and industrial-scale breakthroughs. As a Principal Engineer for Security Architecture, within our Security Engineering organization, you will own a core security domain of the AI factory: the architecture, the paved road that delivers it, and much of the code underneath. You will hold the security design bar across DGX Cloud from inside the teams doing the building, and this is a founding seat on a new team.
Security Engineering is a new organization at DGX Cloud, accountable for the security outcome of the platform, and Security Architecture is the function inside it that holds the design bar. Security here is fleet horizontal and stack vertical, so your work will cross every DGX Cloud engineering organization: you will embed with the teams building GPU clusters, control planes, and services, join their designs as a participant rather than an approver, and leave behind systems in which an entire class of risk is no longer possible. There is no architecture review board here and no approval queue. You are a senior IC with deep security domain knowledge, and the security bar holds because you helped set it and then helped ship it.
What You Will Be Doing:

• Own a Security Domain End to End:Take architectural ownership of a core domain of DGX Cloud security, from the design through the system running in production. That could be tenant and GPU workload isolation, workload identity, infrastructure and network, supply-chain provenance, hardened baselines and patching, or deploy-time policy and admission control.

• Embed with the Teams Building It:Join the design early, write the code, and help land it. The posture is not "you did this wrong." It is "here are the considerations we need to meet, I will help, let's go to work."

• Build Paved Roads, Not Gates:Engineer the secure path into the platform so that it is also the easy path. You are measured by whether teams take that path by default, not by the number of requirements you have written down.

• Engineer Classes of Risk Out of Existence:Finding a vulnerability is 4% of the work; building the system where it cannot happen again is the other 96%. When teams keep missing the same requirement, the paved road is wrong, and fixing the road is our job rather than theirs.

• Threat Model and Attack the Design:Run deep-dive threat models across the substrate, the orchestration layer, and the tenancy boundary, then go after your own designs offensively and feed what you find back into the baselines, the guardrails, and the detections.

• Carry the Bar into Execution:Turn the DGX Cloud security bar into reference architectures, requirements, and golden paths teams can build against. Raise gaps early, in the design, with the work to close them attached.

• Multi-Functional Collaboration:Partner with DGX Cloud platform, production engineering, and network security teams, and with NVIDIA 's central security organization, to make the secure path real in CI/CD and in the hardware lifecycle. title: Automation Engineer I/II, Sustaining Engineering & Lab Operations
description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences is hiring Automation Engineers for the AI Science Factory (AISF), the automated platform behind our work in drug discovery, bioengineering, and advanced materials. You will join Sustaining Engineering & Lab Operations (SELO), the group responsible for keeping the platform running and improving it. You own both halves of that: operating and recovering the workcells through your shift, and developing the changes that make them more reliable and higher throughput.

SELO is a multidisciplinary group of automation, mechanical, and controls engineers, staffed across shifts. Most problems worth your time cross those lines - a scheduling error that turns out to be a sensor, a throughput ceiling that turns out to be a gripper tolerance. You will bring the operational evidence and work the problem with them to a real fix.

The platform runs production across shifts, so improvement work is not something you fit into idle time. You plan it, negotiate the downtime with Research Operations, schedule it into an approved window, and verify the change held before returning the system to service. Doing that well takes as much coordination as engineering.

Handoff is part of the job rather than an afterthought. You give and receive a structured handoff at shift overlap, and document events, decisions, and open issues clearly enough that the other shift can act on them without coming back to you.

This is a full-time, on-site role in Cambridge, MA.

Shifts

This role is shift-based, and we are hiring for both shifts:

• First shift - 7:00 AM-3:00 PM, weekdays

• Second shift - 2:00-10:00 PM, weekdays

The shifts overlap for one hour so the outgoing and incoming engineers can hand off directly. Shift assignments are permanent rather than rotating - you will not be moved between shifts. Both shifts carry the same responsibilities, the same level expectations, and the same development ownership. Let us know your preference when you apply.

What You'll Be Building

• Own operation of the AISF workcells during your shift - triage instrument faults, software errors, and run failures as they surface, recover stalled runs, and decide what gets resolved in shift versus stabilized and carried across the handoff.

• Drive continuous improvement of the systems and workflows you operate: identify where reliability, throughput, or recoverability falls short, propose the change, and see it through implementation and verification.

• Plan improvement and maintenance work around live production - coordinate required downtime with Research Operations, schedule into approved windows, and confirm the change held before returning the system to service.

• Work with SELO mechanical and controls engineers to resolve problems spanning hardware, controls, integration, and software, bringing the operational evidence needed to find root cause.

• Execute preventive maintenance and calibrations on schedule, and coordinate vendor service, parts, and spares for issues in your scope.

• Coordinate with on-shift Research Operations scientists to prioritize recovery when multiple issues compete, and keep active experiments moving with their scientific constraints in view.

• Extend the runbooks, recovery playbooks, and diagnostic tooling the team works from, so the next engineer to hit a recurring problem resolves it faster.

• Document shift events, decisions, and open issues, and run structured handoff in both directions at shift overlap.

• Surface recurring failure patterns and process gaps to SELO so root causes and process weaknesses get addressed rather than absorbed.

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Biology, Chemistry, Materials Science, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience.

• 1+ years of hands-on experience with lab automation, lab instrumentation, or production operations in a life sciences or physical sciences environment.

• Ability to troubleshoot electro-mech

title: Technical Project Manager - SAP Deployment
description:
The Technical Project Manager - SAP Deployment is responsible for coordinating and driving the technical and operational activities required to successfully deploy the Project Elevate SAP solution to BFS field locations. This position serves as a key connection point between Deployment Field Services, the Deployment Hub, Core Project teams, Business Enablement, site leadership, SAP functional/technical teams, Security, Data, Training, and support organizations. The role drives deployment readiness, manages dependencies and risks, coordinates cutover and Hypercare activities, and ensures technical issues are identified, routed, tracked, and resolved through the appropriate teams. The position is not intended to be an SAP configuration/development role. Rather, the Technical Project Manager must understand SAP-enabled business processes and the BFS deployment model well enough to identify dependencies, facilitate technical problem solving, manage cross-functional execution, and communicate clearly between technical teams and field/site operations. Key Responsibilities

• Deployment Planning & Execution
Lead team readiness and SAP functional training, ensuring team members develop the knowledge, skills, and hands-on proficiency required to confidently support their assigned functional area during deployment, go-live, and Hypercare. Prepare and coach team members for effective end-user support, reinforcing strong communication, patience, professionalism, problem-solving, and a positive, customer-focused attitude when working with end users. Drive go-live and Hypercare readiness, keeping the team focused, engaged, and accountable while monitoring training progress, addressing knowledge gaps, reinforcing key processes, and ensuring the team is prepared to provide effective on-site support under demanding deployment conditions. Develop and maintain detailed deployment plans for assigned SAP deployment waves and locations. Coordinate technical activities across pre-deployment, readiness, cutover, go-live, Hypercare, and transition-to-support phases. Coordinate activities across multiple BFS locations and deployment workstreams. Ensure owners, due dates, dependencies, and escalation paths are clearly established. Identify schedule conflicts and critical-path risks early and drive them toward resolution.

• Technical & Site Readiness
Coordinate and track readiness of technical dependencies required for successful field deployment, including applicable:
SAP environment/access readiness User roles and security access Site and deployment data readiness Devices and handheld technology Infrastructure and connectivity dependencies Interfaces and application dependencies Training/practice environments Deployment and support tools Build effective working relationships with BFS site leaders and field teams

• Cutover & Go-Live Coordination
Coordinate Field Deployment activities associated with production cutover and go-live. Maintain visibility to critical cutover tasks, dependencies, owners, status, and blockers. Facilitate deployment checkpoints and escalation discussions. Coordinate with Deployment Hub, Core Project, business, technical, and field resources when cutover activities affect site readiness. Ensure issues discovered during deployment are routed to the appropriate owner rather than allowing field teams to develop unsupported workarounds. Translate field operational issues into information technical and functional teams can act upon. Help technical teams understand the real-world business impact of deployment issues. Maintain focus on business continuity during deployment. Promote adoption of standard BFS Way processes rather than unsupported local workarounds.

• Hypercare & Incident Coordination
Support operational stabilization after SAP go-live. Monitor deployment issues and incidents requiring cross-team coordination. Drive appropriate triage and escalation of technical, functional, data, access, integration, or process issues.

description:
Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services has made life harder for them - with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that.

We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe - one built around simple tools, thoughtful design and real human support. Our Members rely on us to help them run their business with confidence, and that responsibility shapes the way we work.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you want to build meaningful products, solve real problems and make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you

TO BE A TEYAN

We are not just a fintech company. We develop people by giving them the autonomy and the responsibility to challenge the status quo, so they can be the main actors of the change we want to bring to the market.

We are always looking for people better than us to join the team, disrupt payments, and revolutionise commerce in Europe. The goal we share, the mission is one, and at the end of the day we are just people trying to help other people.

WHAT IS YOUR MISSION?

Our sales agents are on the front lines, talking to merchants every day. Across the go to market systems they use to manage their sales, HubSpot CRM is where their deals, activities, conversations, reporting, automations and portfolio lives. When HubSpot works, our salespeople sell. When it breaks quietly in the background, deals stall, data drifts, and the people who trust the numbers stop trusting the tool.

Your mission is to be the guardian of that system. You are the person who keeps HubSpot healthy, honest, and trustworthy, so that every seller and every leader can rely on it without ever thinking about it.

This is not a caretaking job where you wait for tickets and tick them off. You are a detective and a builder. You go looking for what is wrong before anyone reports it, you find the real reason something failed instead of patching the symptom, and you make sure the same failure never happens twice. You turn a messy, growing CRM into a system people can trust, and you can prove it with data.

AS THE GUARDIAN OF OUR CRM YOU WILL

Investigate root causes, not symptoms. When something in HubSpot fails, you own it. You dig into what actually went wrong, validate the real root cause, and drive it to a fix. You are the single point of contact when the CRM misbehaves, and nothing gets dropped on your watch.

Prevent the next bug before it happens. You do not just close errors, you learn from them. You spot the patterns, harden the implementations that keep breaking, and put guardrails in place so a whole class of problems disappears. Every automation and implementation, local or global, follows our guidelines because you make sure it does, before and after it goes live.

Measure the health of the CRM. You build the dashboards that show, at a glance, whether what we ship actually works and keeps working. You track error rates, adoption, and data quality over time, so CRM health stops being a feeling and becomes a number we can watch and improve.

Turn data into action. You are as comfortable reading the numbers as fixing the system. You globalise and clean up our reporting once the requirements from Commercial Excellence are aligned, retire the dashboards no one needs, and use data to find the problems no one has noticed yet.

Build and improve, hands on. You create new automations and refine the ones we have, you read the logic of a workflow well enough to debug it, and you keep the instance clean, governed, and scalable across every market in Europe.

title: Global Program Manager
description:
Global Program Manager
The Global Program Manager or GPM will be the primary contact for specific qualified accounts that is accountable for overall program health, maturation, governance, and supporting growth opportunities. The GPM will gain alignment with key stakeholders within their assigned customers to ensure customer health is established by establishing short and long-term objectives that align with the Trax Value Pyramid and the associated methods to achieve those objectives. The GPM will also align with the customer around KPIs and metrics as a method to measure program and make necessary program changes when needed. Successful execution of a customer program will be measured using specific KPIs and their associated targets, avoiding revenue churn, and support overall account growth by working with their sales counterpart building a business case for program augmentation. The GPM will closely work with all support team members as a customer advocate internal to the Trax organization but also manage governance to contractual obligations. The GPM be accountable for monthly business reviews and collaborate on quarterly business reviews for each assigned customer in their portfolio.
Core Skills Required

• Verbal and non-Verbal Communication
The GPM must be able to verbally and non-verbally communicate with both operational (tactical) and strategic customer stakeholders to understand customer requirements, escalations, and objectives and contractual obligations.

title: Co-Founder & CEO - AI Retail Planning Autopilot
description:
The Opportunity
FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Foundry, an AI-Native Recruiting Agency currently in build at FutureSight . This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.
Recruiting has run on the same model for decades: firms charge a fixed percentage of a hire's first-year salary for work that is largely manual, sourcing, screening, and outreach done one candidate at a time. That pricing made sense when the work required a person doing it by hand. It doesn't anymore.
Market Context
Foundry is an AI-native recruiting firm built around a simple idea: use AI agents to handle sourcing, screening, and candidate evaluation, and keep a small human team focused on what still requires a person: building trust with clients and candidates, exercising judgment on close calls, and closing the placement. That shift in who does the work lets us offer clients a fee that's a fraction of what traditional firms charge, without cutting corners on quality.
This is where we believe recruiting is headed. AI-native service firms are starting to emerge and prove the model works, and we're building toward that shift deliberately.
About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.
You’ll co-create with a proven studio team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.
The Partnership

• Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception

• Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding

• Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one

• Investor and advisor network across vertical AI and early-stage capital markets

• A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight 's cross-functional team as your partner

What you'll own
As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead its execution.

• Strategy - Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning

• Customer Development - Lead pilot placements with design-partner companies, convert them to paid retained relationships, and build the go-to-market motion

• Product - Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback

• Capital - Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight 's network and traction

• Team - Recruit and lead the founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

• Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company

• Demonstrated success in B2B AI or B2B SaaS go-to-market, including consultative, relationship-driven sales and customer engagement

• Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital

• Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent

• Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company

• Deep domain expertise in recruiting, staffing, or talent acquisition, as a builder operator or agency leader

How to Apply
Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.
FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

title: HR Business Partner, GTM
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The HRBP team at OpenAI partners with leaders on complex organizational and talent decisions where the right path isn’t always obvious. We stay close to the business so we understand its realities, and focus our time where judgment, influence, and context can make the biggest difference: improving decisions, strengthening leaders, and helping teams work better.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Go-to-Market HR Business Partner, you’ll be a trusted advisor, sounding board, and hands-on problem solver for leaders in your client group. This is an individual contributor role. You’ll help leaders decide how to organize, grow, and lead their teams, bringing a point of view on the tradeoffs rather than simply executing the first request.

That starts with understanding the business problem. If customer coverage needs to change, for example, you’ll help leaders clarify what’s driving the change, weigh options for team structure and staffing, and work with them to put the decision into practice. The goal is to leave leaders better equipped to make the next decision, too.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

- Help GTM leaders make better decisions about team structure, workforce plans, and hiring. Work with Finance and Recruiting to turn those decisions into plans the business can execute.

- Build leadership capability by giving candid, actionable feedback and coaching managers through complex performance, development, and succession decisions.

- Lead the people side of organizational changes, from planning and communication to clarifying roles and supporting teams through transitions.

- Work with regional HRBPs and People partners, including Compensation and Employee Relations, to apply consistent practices while accounting for local needs.

- Use workforce data, employee feedback, and business context to spot issues early, test assumptions, and track progress.

- Build simple systems and routines that help GTM teams scale. Improve how leaders review talent, spot emerging issues, and follow through on decisions.

YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

- Have partnered with senior leaders as an HRBP in a fast-growing technology organization, with direct experience supporting Sales, Revenue, Customer Success, or a related GTM function.

- Understand how customer-facing teams are structured and how shifts in growth, customer coverage, or operating models affect what those teams need.

- Have led org design, workforce planning, talent reviews, or significant organizational change and can show how you turned a plan into action.

- Build trust quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and influence decisions without relying on formal authority.

- Build trust with senior leaders, ask questions that get to the root of the problem, and challenge assumptions with care. You can lay out options, explain the tradeoffs, and influence decisions without formal authority.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.
